title: The Civil War split
hook: Secession, slavery and military geography divided the union.
notes: Original Orbis factual synthesis; linked federal records and historic-site accounts, checked 14 October 2026. Points locate places approximately, not territorial extents. Modern national/state outlines are reference geography, never reconstructed historical borders. No archival images or source prose redistributed. Sources by scene: State affiliation was not control: https://www.nps.gov/anti/learn/historyculture/roadtoseccession.htm; War begins at a harbour fort: https://www.nps.gov/civilwar/search-battles-detail.htm?battleCode=SC001; The border states complicate the split: https://www.nps.gov/articles/the-border-states.htm; Emancipation had a geographic limit: https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/emancipation-proclamation; Appomattox was one surrender: https://www.nps.gov/appomattoxcourthouse Supplementary date/location evidence: https://www.nps.gov/civilwar/facts.htm; https://www.nps.gov/apco/learn/historyculture/surrender-events-after-appomattox.htm. Affiliations follow NPS Civil War facts and Border States; modern outlines are reference geometry. West Virginia is omitted because it was part of Virginia in 1861. Affiliations are not military-control polygons; Kentucky and Missouri had rival Confederate governments.

scenes.title: State affiliation was not control
scenes.text: Slavery was central to secession. This late-1861 affiliation map uses modern state outlines; it does not map occupation or unanimity. West Virginia is omitted because it was then part of Virginia.

scenes.title: War begins at a harbour fort
scenes.text: Confederate forces opened fire on Fort Sumter on 12 April 1861. Charleston Harbour locates the attack that began the war; the point does not describe the later Union blockade.

scenes.title: The border states complicate the split
scenes.text: Delaware, Maryland, Kentucky and Missouri retained slavery while remaining in the Union. Rival loyalties and fighting inside these states make a simple North–South colour divide misleading.

scenes.title: Emancipation had a geographic limit
scenes.text: The Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 applied to areas in rebellion, with specified exemptions. It did not itself abolish slavery everywhere in the United States; Washington locates the issuing government.

scenes.title: Appomattox was one surrender
scenes.text: Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia at Appomattox on 9 April 1865. The surrender was a major endpoint, but other Confederate armies surrendered later.
